items.prompt: Where is Dilnoza from?
items.audio:
Hello! My name is Dilnoza. I am eleven years old, and I am from Samarkand. Today is my first day at your school, and I am a little nervous. I want to tell you about myself so we can be friends.

I live with my mother, my father and my little sister. My sister is called Malika. She is six years old and she loves cats. We have one cat at home. Her name is Mushuk, which means cat in Uzbek. My mother is a doctor in a small clinic. My father drives a bus in the city. They both work very hard, but we always eat dinner together at seven o'clock.

My favourite subject is art. I like to draw flowers and birds. I also like swimming. Every Saturday I go to the pool with my cousin at ten o'clock. I cannot play football, but I would like to learn.

My best colour is green, and my favourite food is plov.

Now I want to know about you. What is your name? Do you have brothers or sisters? What do you like to do after school? Maybe we can sit together at lunch tomorrow. I have an apple and a sandwich, and I can share them with you. Thank you for listening, and I hope to see you soon!

items.prompt: Who is seventy years old?
items.audio:
Welcome to my home! My name is Sardor, and today I will show you my family.

In the middle you can see my grandfather. His name is Karim, and he is seventy years old. He has white hair and a kind face. Next to him is my grandmother, Halima. She makes the best bread in our street.

On the left is my father, Anvar. He is a teacher of maths. He is tall and he wears glasses. My mother, Feruza, is standing next to him. She works in a shop that sells shoes. She comes home at five o'clock every day.

Now look at the children. The tall boy is my older brother, Jamshid. He is fifteen and he plays the guitar. The girl in the red dress is my sister, Nilufar. She is nine, and she is very funny. She loves to dance. And the small boy at the front is me! I am twelve years old, and I like computers.

We also have a dog in the garden. His name is Bars, and he is two years old. He is brown and very friendly.

Every Friday, all of us have lunch together in the big room. We talk, we laugh and we eat soup. I love my family very much. Now, would you like some tea?

items.prompt: Who gave Emma the name of her pen friend?
items.audio:
Hi Jasur! This is Emma from England. This is my first voice message to you, and I am very happy to be your pen friend. My teacher gave me your name last week.

I am twelve years old, and I live in a small town near London. My house is next to a park, and I walk there with my dog every morning. His name is Max. He is a white dog with one black ear. He is very noisy!

I live with my mum, my dad and my brother Oliver. Oliver is seven. He likes football and he plays all day. My mum works in a library, so she knows many good books. My dad is a bus driver, and he starts work very early, at five o'clock in the morning.

At school, my best subject is English, of course, but I also like science. My worst subject is maths. I have three good friends in my class. Their names are Lucy, Sophie and Ben. After school we often go to the cafe and drink hot chocolate.

I want to learn about your country. Do you have a big family? What food do you like? Please tell me about the city of Tashkent. I also want to learn a few words in Uzbek. How do you say hello?

items.prompt: How old is Zulfiya now?
items.audio:
Come and sit near me, children. Today I will tell you about my life when I was small. My name is Zulfiya, and I am seventy-two years old now. But once I was a little girl, just like you.

I was born in a village near Fergana. We had a small house with a big garden. My father worked in the fields, and my mother made bread every morning. I had four brothers and one sister, so our house was always full of people. We did not have a television, and we did not have a telephone. But we were happy.

Every day I walked to school with my sister. The school was far away, and the walk took one hour. In winter the road was cold and white, and our feet were wet. My teacher was a kind woman called Miss Saida. She taught me to read and write, and I still remember her face.

After school I helped my mother. I fed the chickens, and I carried water from the well. In the evening my grandfather told us stories by the fire.

When I was twenty, I met your grandfather at a wedding. He was shy and he gave me a red apple. One year later we got married. Now we have six grandchildren, and that is the best gift of my life.

items.prompt: Which floor is Gulnora's new flat on?
items.audio:
Gulnora has just moved to a new flat on the third floor. On Saturday morning she carries a box up the stairs, and she meets a woman at the door next to hers. The woman smiles and says hello.

The woman says, "Hello! My name is Mrs Brown. I am your new neighbour. Welcome to the building!" Gulnora says, "Thank you. My name is Gulnora. Nice to meet you." Mrs Brown asks, "Are you from this city?" Gulnora answers, "No, I come from Namangan. I am a student of medicine, and I study at the university near here."

Mrs Brown tells her about the building. She says that the shop on the corner opens at eight o'clock and closes at nine o'clock in the evening. The best bakery is behind the bus stop. The lift does not work, so everyone uses the stairs.

Mrs Brown is sixty years old, and she lives with her cat, Lily. Her son lives in Canada, and he calls her every Sunday. She likes gardening, and she has many flowers on her balcony.

Then Mrs Brown says, "Would you like to have tea with me tomorrow at four o'clock?" Gulnora is very happy. She says, "Yes, please. I will bring some sweets from my home town." They say goodbye, and Gulnora feels much better in her new home.

items.prompt: Where does Kamola work?
items.audio:
Hello, children. Thank you for inviting me to your class. My name is Kamola, and I am a nurse. Today I want to tell you about my job.

I work in a children's hospital in the centre of the city. I start work at seven o'clock in the morning, and I finish at three o'clock in the afternoon. I wear a white coat and a small blue hat, and I always keep a pen in my pocket.

What do I do every day? First, I say good morning to the children in the hospital. Then I take their temperature and check their pulse. I give them medicine, and I write everything in a big book. I also help the doctors. When a child is afraid, I sit with him, and I tell him a story or sing a song. This is the best part of my work.

To be a nurse, you need to study for four years. You must also be kind, patient and calm. You must wash your hands many times a day. That is very important because it stops germs.

I work with eight other nurses and five doctors. At lunch we eat soup and bread together. I love my job because I help people every day. If you want to be a nurse one day, work hard at school. Are there any questions?

items.prompt: What is Nigora's job in the club?
items.audio:
Hello, everybody! My name is Nigora, and I am the leader of the school chess club. Today I want to invite you to join us. Chess is a fun game, and anyone can learn it.

Our club started three years ago. At first there were only five members, but now we have twenty-eight. We meet every Wednesday after lessons, at half past two, in room number twelve. The meeting lasts one hour. We have eight boards, so students play in pairs.

In the first part of the meeting, I teach a new idea. For example, last week I showed the little children how a horse moves. After that, we play games, and we drink tea and eat biscuits. Our teacher, Mr Rustam, helps us when we have questions. He plays chess very well, and he once won a big prize in Tashkent.

Chess is good for your brain. It teaches you to think slowly and to be patient. It also teaches you to lose without being sad. I lost my first twenty games, but I did not stop, and now I am the best player in the school.

In May, we will have a tournament with another school. The winner will get a silver cup. Just come to room twelve next Wednesday and say hello. I promise you will have fun!

items.prompt: Where does Bobur live?
items.audio:
Last week my cousin Bobur came to visit us. He lives in the city of Khiva, and he stayed with us for five days. I was very happy because I had not seen him for a year.

Bobur arrived on Monday morning by train. My father met him at the station at nine o'clock. Bobur had a big green bag and a present for me. The present was a box of dried apricots from his mother, my aunt Sevara. She makes them every summer.

Bobur is fourteen years old, two years older than I am. He is thin and very funny. He can make an animal sound with his mouth, and he made my little sister laugh all the time. He also speaks a little Russian and some English, and he helped me with my English homework.

On Tuesday we took him to the big market. He bought a hat for his father and a scarf for his mother. On Wednesday we went to the park and rode bicycles. I fell off mine, but I was not hurt. On Thursday my mother cooked a special dinner with rice, meat and carrots, and the whole family sat together.

On Friday afternoon, he went home. I felt sad at the station. Bobur said, "Next time, you must come to Khiva." I said yes.

Dear family and friends, thank you for coming to my daughter's party. Today is a very special day. Madina is ten years old! I am her father, and I want to say a few words.

Ten years ago, on a cold morning in January, I held Madina for the first time. She was very small, and she had a lot of black hair. I looked at her, and I was the happiest man in the world. Her mother cried, and so did I.

When Madina was two, she began to talk. Her first word was not mum or dad. It was cat! We still laugh about that. At four, she learned to ride a bicycle. At six, she started school, and her backpack was bigger than she was. Now she is in the fourth class, and her teacher says she is one of the best readers.

Madina is a kind girl. She shares her sweets, she helps her little brother with his shoes, and she always says thank you. She loves to sing, and she is learning the piano. Maybe one day she will play for the whole country.

Madina, my dear, we love you very much. May you always be healthy and happy. Now, please, everybody, stand up, and let us sing together. After that, we will eat the big chocolate cake that her grandmother made. Happy birthday, Madina!

items.prompt: What day is it?
items.audio:
It is Sunday afternoon, and Sevara is at home with her grandmother. Suddenly someone knocks at the door. Sevara opens it and sees a young man with a red bag. He smiles and says, "Hello! Is this the home of Mr Aliev?"

Sevara says, "Yes, it is. He is my grandfather. But he is not at home now. He is at the market." The young man says, "Oh, I see. My name is Tom. I come from England. I am a friend of his son, Farhod. Farhod told me to visit his father when I was in town."

Sevara asks, "Are you tired? Please come in. Would you like some water or tea?" Tom says, "Tea, please. Thank you very much." Sevara takes him to the living room, and her grandmother brings green tea, bread and sweets. She smiles and says, "You are welcome in our house."

Tom takes a small box from his bag. He says, "This is a present from Farhod. It is a watch." Grandmother says, "How kind! My husband will be very happy."

After twenty minutes, Mr Aliev comes back from the market with a big melon. He is surprised to see a stranger, but he quickly understands. He hugs Tom and says, "You must stay for dinner tonight." Tom laughs and says, "With pleasure!"

My name is Otabek, and I want to talk about my hero. My hero is my uncle Rahim. He is a firefighter, and he works in the city of Andijan.

My uncle is thirty-eight years old. He is tall and strong, and he has a loud, warm voice. He wears a yellow helmet and heavy boots at work. His red truck is very big, and he lets me sit in it when I visit him.

Why is he my hero? Two years ago, there was a fire in a house near our street. It was late at night. The family was inside, and they could not get out. My uncle came with his team. He went into the house and carried out a small girl and her grandmother. Then he went back for their cat! The next day, the mayor gave him a medal.

But my uncle says he is not special. He says it is just his job. He also says that a hero is someone who helps others without waiting for thanks.

My uncle works two days and then rests for two days. On his days off, he visits schools and tells children how to stay safe. He says, "Never play with matches, and always know two ways out of your home." I always remember these words. One day I want to be a firefighter, like him.

items.prompt: How long has Rustam been a driver?
items.audio:
Hello, my name is Rustam, and I am a taxi driver in Tashkent. I am forty years old, and I have been a driver for twelve years. Let me tell you about my day.

I get up at five o'clock in the morning. I drink a cup of black tea and eat a piece of bread with honey. Then I check my car. It is a small white car, and I wash it every second day. I leave home at six o'clock.

In the morning, many people go to work, so I am very busy. I take them to offices, schools and the railway station. I like to talk with my customers. Some are sleepy and quiet, but others are happy and tell me about their lives. Once a woman told me a funny story about her parrot. It could say my name!

At twelve o'clock I stop for lunch. I usually eat in a small cafe near the market. I have rice with meat and a salad. After lunch I rest for twenty minutes, and then I work again until seven o'clock in the evening.

The hardest part of my job is the traffic. In the afternoon, the streets are full of cars, and I wait a long time.

I come home at eight o'clock. I play with my daughter and have dinner with my wife.

items.prompt: What is the cafe called?
items.audio:
It is Saturday morning, and Dilnoza goes to a small cafe near her house. The cafe is called Green Cup. It is warm inside, and a soft song plays on the radio. Dilnoza sits at a table by the window. A young waiter named Bobur comes with a menu. He smiles and says good morning. Dilnoza says good morning too. She is very hungry because she did not eat breakfast at home.

First she asks for a cup of black tea with two spoons of sugar. Then she looks at the menu for a long time. She wants something sweet, but she also wants something warm. At last she orders an omelette with cheese and a small salad. She also asks for two pieces of brown bread. Bobur writes everything on a small paper. He says the food will be ready in ten minutes.

While she waits, Dilnoza calls her friend Madina. Madina is coming to the cafe at ten o'clock. They want to plan a trip to the mountains. Soon Bobur brings the tea and the omelette. The omelette smells very good. Dilnoza eats slowly and enjoys it. When Madina arrives, she orders a cup of coffee and an apple cake. The bill is thirty thousand soms. Dilnoza pays, says thank you, and leaves a small tip for Bobur.

items.prompt: When does the market open?
items.audio:
On Sunday morning, Jasur goes to the big market with his mother. The market opens at seven o'clock, and it is already full of people. There are many small shops with fruit, vegetables, meat, and bread. The air smells of fresh herbs and warm bread. Jasur carries two big bags for his mother.

First they go to the vegetable shop. A kind woman named Zebo sells them two kilos of tomatoes and one kilo of onions. The tomatoes are red and very fresh. Jasur's mother also buys three kilos of potatoes. She asks the price, and Zebo says it is twelve thousand soms. His mother thinks it is a little high, so she asks for a cheaper price. Zebo smiles and agrees.

Next, they visit the fruit seller. Jasur wants a watermelon because it is hot today. They find a big, round one, and the seller cuts a small piece for them to try. It is sweet and cold. They buy it at once. Finally, they go to the bakery and take four loaves of warm bread. Jasur is tired, but he is happy. They go home by bus at eleven o'clock, and his mother makes a big lunch for the family.

items.prompt: Why does Kamola need a jacket?
items.audio:
Kamola needs a new jacket because winter is coming. After school on Wednesday, she goes to a clothes shop in the city centre. The shop is bright and big. There are many shirts, skirts, shoes, and coats. A shop assistant named Gulnara comes to help her. She asks, "Can I help you?" Kamola says she wants a warm jacket in red or blue.

Gulnara shows her three jackets. The first one is red, but it is too small. Kamola needs size medium, and this one is size small. The second one is black and too expensive. It costs two hundred thousand soms. The third jacket is dark blue, and it looks perfect. Kamola goes to the changing room and tries it on. It is warm, soft, and very comfortable.

She asks about the price. Gulnara says it was eighty thousand soms, but today there is a twenty percent discount. Kamola is very happy. She also looks at some white gloves and a grey hat. She buys the gloves too, but she does not buy the hat. At the cash desk, she pays with her card. Gulnara puts everything in a paper bag. Kamola thanks her and says she will come again soon.

items.prompt: When is Rustam's father's birthday?
items.audio:

Mr. Brown is a tourist from London. Tonight he is at a restaurant in Samarkand, and he does not know the food. A friendly waitress named Sevara brings him the menu. She says, "Let me explain the dishes." Mr. Brown is happy because he is very hungry.

Sevara says the first dish is plov. It is the most famous dish in Uzbekistan. It is made with rice, meat, carrots, and onions. It is hot and a little oily, and people eat it for lunch or dinner. Next is shurpa. This is a soup with beef, potatoes, and vegetables. It is good on a cold evening. Then she points to samsa. Samsa is a small pie with meat inside, and cooks bake it in a special oven. Last, there is lagman, a dish with long noodles, meat, and spicy sauce.

Mr. Brown asks what the best dish is for a beginner. Sevara says plov is the best choice. He also orders a pot of green tea and a plate of fresh bread. Sevara says the food will arrive in fifteen minutes. When she comes back, Mr. Brown tastes the plov and says it is delicious. He asks for the recipe, but Sevara laughs and says the chef keeps it secret.

items.prompt: What time does Hamid wake up?
items.audio:
Hamid is a baker, and his day starts very early. He wakes up at four o'clock in the morning, when the city is still dark and quiet. He walks ten minutes to the bakery and turns on the lights. First he washes his hands and puts on a white apron. Then he makes the dough with flour, water, salt, and a little sugar.

At five o'clock, his helper Otabek arrives. Otabek is nineteen years old, and he is learning the work. Together they make round loaves and small buns. Hamid puts them into a big clay oven called a tandoor. The oven is very hot, and the bread smells wonderful after a few minutes. Hamid takes out each loaf with a long wooden tool.

The shop opens at six o'clock. The first customer is an old lady who buys two loaves every day. Then come students, workers, and mothers with small children. Many people ask for warm bread with sesame seeds on top. By nine o'clock, Hamid sells almost one hundred loaves. He is tired, but he loves his job. At noon, he closes the door, drinks a cup of tea, and eats a sweet bun. In the afternoon, he goes home and sleeps for two hours.

items.prompt: Hamid sleeps in the afternoon.
items.audio:
Hamid is a baker, and his day starts very early. He wakes up at four o'clock in the morning, when the city is still dark and quiet. He walks ten minutes to the bakery and turns on the lights. First he washes his hands and puts on a white apron. Then he makes the dough with flour, water, salt, and a little sugar.

At five o'clock, his helper Otabek arrives. Otabek is nineteen years old, and he is learning the work. Together they make round loaves and small buns. Hamid puts them into a big clay oven called a tandoor. The oven is very hot, and the bread smells wonderful after a few minutes. Hamid takes out each loaf with a long wooden tool.

The shop opens at six o'clock. The first customer is an old lady who buys two loaves every day. Then come students, workers, and mothers with small children. Many people ask for warm bread with sesame seeds on top. By nine o'clock, Hamid sells almost one hundred loaves. He is tired, but he loves his job. At noon, he closes the door, drinks a cup of tea, and eats a sweet bun. In the afternoon, he goes home and sleeps for two hours.

items.prompt: What is the pizza shop called?
items.audio:
It is Friday evening, and Nigora is at home with her two brothers. They are hungry, but nobody wants to cook. Nigora decides to call a pizza shop called Mario's. A young man answers the phone and says, "Good evening. Mario's Pizza. How can I help you?"

Nigora says she wants one large pizza with chicken and mushrooms. The young man asks if she wants extra cheese. She says yes, please. Her little brother Sardor wants a small pizza with only tomato and cheese, so she orders that too. Then the young man asks about drinks. Nigora orders one big bottle of orange juice and two cans of cola. He says the total price is ninety thousand soms.

Next, he asks for her address. Nigora gives the street name, house number, and her phone number. The house is the yellow one next to the pharmacy. The young man says the delivery takes thirty minutes. Nigora can pay with cash or by card, and she chooses cash. She says thank you and ends the call.

At exactly seven thirty, the doorbell rings. The delivery boy is polite, and the pizzas are still hot. The three children sit together, eat, and watch a funny film. Sardor says it is the best pizza ever.

Please remember that plastic bags are not free today. We have strong paper bags at the cash desk, and they cost only five hundred soms. Better still, bring your own bag from home. It is good for our city.

items.prompt: What is the name of the teacher?
items.audio:
Welcome to our cooking class. My name is Chef Olga, and today we make pancakes. They are easy, quick, and everybody loves them. First, please wash your hands and put on an apron.

Let us look at the things we need. You need two eggs, two cups of flour, two cups of milk, one spoon of sugar, and a little salt. You also need some butter for the pan.

Step one. Take a big bowl and break the eggs into it. Be careful with the shells. Step two. Add the milk and mix well with a fork. Step three. Slowly add the flour, a little at a time. Mix until the dough is smooth and there are no lumps. Then add the sugar and the salt. Let the dough rest for ten minutes.

Now we cook. Put a pan on the stove and make it hot. Add a small piece of butter. Pour some dough into the pan, and move the pan so the dough is thin and round. Wait for about one minute. When the edge is golden, turn the pancake over with a spatula. Cook it for another thirty seconds.

Finally, put the pancakes on a plate. You can eat them with honey, jam, or fruit. Please enjoy your lunch, and do not forget to clean the table.

items.prompt: Why is Timur's father busy?
items.audio:
It is Saturday, and Timur's father is very busy in the garden. He asks Timur to go to the shop and buy some food for the weekend. He reads the list slowly, and Timur listens carefully. Then Timur writes everything on a piece of paper.

First, they need bread. Timur must buy two loaves of white bread. Second, they need one litre of milk and a box of ten eggs. Third, Father wants a kilo of rice and one packet of green tea. For dinner tonight, Mother wants to make soup, so Timur must also buy four potatoes, three carrots, and one big onion. For dessert, he must buy a kilo of red apples and some bananas.

Father says Timur must not forget the butter. It is small, yellow, and it is near the milk. He gives Timur a hundred thousand soms and says the change is for him. Timur must not buy sweets or chocolate because there are some at home.

Timur takes his bag and walks to the shop. It is only five minutes from the house. In the shop, he finds everything easily. At the cash desk, the woman says the total is seventy thousand soms. Timur takes the change and runs home happily. Father says, "Well done, my son."

items.prompt: Where is Karim's stall?
items.audio:
My name is Karim, and I am a fruit seller. I have a small stall near the bus station. I sell fruit every day from seven in the morning to six in the evening. My work is hard, but I love it. I meet many kind people, and I always say hello with a smile.

Today I have apricots, grapes, melons, and peaches. The apricots come from my cousin's garden in Fergana. They are small, orange, and very sweet. One kilo costs twenty thousand soms. The grapes are green and have no seeds, so children love them. The melons are big and yellow. I always tell my customers to smell the melon first. A good melon has a sweet smell.

In the morning, a young woman named Feruza comes to my stall. She wants fruit for her little daughter. I give her two peaches to try, and she says they are delicious. She buys one kilo of peaches and half a kilo of grapes. I give her a small bag of apricots as a present. She is very happy and says she will come again tomorrow.

In the evening, I wash the stall, cover the fruit, and count the money. Then I take the last bus home. My wife has dinner ready for me, and I sleep well.

Next Sunday is Sherzod's twelfth birthday, and his mother, Malika, plans a special dinner at home. She wants everything to be perfect. On Monday evening, she sits at the kitchen table with a pen and a notebook. She writes the names of the guests first. It is a wonderful evening, and Sherzod says it is the best birthday of his life.

items.prompt: Who did Ali visit the tea house with?
items.audio:
Last Friday, Ali visited a traditional tea house with his grandfather. In Uzbek, it is called a chaikhana. It stands under a huge old tree in the middle of a quiet park. Ali was very excited because it was his first time there.

They took off their shoes and sat on a big wooden platform covered with soft red carpets. A friendly man in a small black hat brought them a blue teapot and two small bowls. He poured green tea and said, "Please enjoy." Ali's grandfather explained the custom. You pour the tea into the bowl three times and then pour it back into the pot. After that, the tea tastes better.

The man also brought a plate of flat bread, a bowl of sweet raisins, and some sugar candies. Ali ate the bread with honey and drank two bowls of tea. Around them, old men played chess and talked about the weather. Somewhere, a musician played a long guitar-like instrument, and the music was calm and slow.

They stayed there for two hours. Ali's grandfather told him stories about the old days. When the sun went down, they paid twenty thousand soms and walked home slowly. Ali said, "Grandfather, let us come again next Friday."

items.prompt: When is the festival every year?
items.audio:
Every year in September, our city has a big food festival in Central Park. This year it is on Saturday and Sunday, from ten in the morning until eight in the evening. The tickets cost only five thousand soms, and children under six enter for free.

There are more than fifty stalls at the festival. Cooks from ten countries bring their national dishes. You can try Japanese sushi, Italian pasta, Turkish kebab, Indian curry, and of course our own Uzbek plov. At the sweet corner, you can taste ice cream, honey cakes, and hot chocolate. A man from Korea will show everybody how to make spicy cabbage, and the lesson starts at two o'clock.

There is also a children's area with a small stage. On Saturday afternoon, a clown will make balloon animals, and children can paint their faces. On Sunday, there is a cooking game for families. The winner gets a big basket of fruit and a new frying pan.

Music plays all day, and there are many places to sit under the trees. Please bring your own bottle for water, because water is free at three points in the park. Buses number five and twelve stop near the main gate. We hope to see you there!

items.prompt: Where does Anna stand at the beginning?
items.answer: In front of the railway station
items.audio:
Anna is new in the town of Bukhara. She stands in front of the railway station on a sunny Monday morning. She needs a bank because she wants to change some money. She asks a young policeman, Mr Karim, for help. Anna says, Excuse me, where is the bank, please? Mr Karim smiles and answers, It is not far. It is only ten minutes on foot.

First, go straight along Navoi Street. Walk past the big supermarket and the small flower shop. At the second traffic light, turn left. Then you will see a green park on your right. Go on for about two hundred metres. The bank is next to the library, opposite a pharmacy. It is a tall white building with a blue door.

Anna asks, Is the bank open now? Mr Karim looks at his watch. He says, Yes, it opens at nine o'clock and it closes at five. Today is Monday, so it is open all day. On Sunday it is closed. Anna says thank you very much. Mr Karim says, You are welcome. Have a nice day. Anna walks to the bank and finds it easily. She is happy because the policeman was kind and the bank is just where he said.

items.prompt: What is the number of the bus?
items.audio:
Good morning, everybody. This is your driver, Rustam, speaking. Welcome to bus number twelve. This bus goes from the market to the city centre. The trip takes thirty minutes. Today the weather is cold, so please keep the windows closed. We hope you have a pleasant ride with us this morning.

Our first stop is School Street. The second stop is the hospital, and the third stop is the football stadium. After the stadium, we stop at the big museum. Please do not forget your bags when you get off. If you want to stop the bus, press the red button near the door. Children under seven travel free. A ticket for an adult costs two thousand som.

Please give your seat to old people and to mothers with babies. Do not eat hot food on the bus. Please do not talk loudly on the phone. The last stop is the central square. We arrive there at a quarter past nine. The next bus leaves at ten o'clock. Thank you for travelling with us, and have a lovely day. If you have a question, please come and ask me at the last stop.

items.prompt: When does Dilnoza arrive at the airport?
items.audio:
Dilnoza arrives at the airport at six in the evening. She is tired and she has two heavy bags. She takes a yellow taxi. The driver is a friendly man called Bobur. He puts the bags in the back of the car. Dilnoza says, Good evening. Please take me to the Grand Hotel on Mustaqillik Street. Bobur says, No problem. It is about twenty minutes from here.

On the way, Bobur asks, Is this your first visit to the city? Dilnoza answers, Yes, I come from Khiva. I want to see the old market and the blue mosque. Bobur says, You must visit the market on Saturday, because it is very big. He also tells her about a good restaurant near the hotel. It serves plov and fresh bread. There is a lot of traffic, so the taxi is slow.

At last they arrive at the hotel. The price is thirty thousand som. Dilnoza gives him forty thousand and says, Keep the change. Bobur is very happy. He gives her his phone card and says, Call me if you need a taxi. Dilnoza thanks him, takes her bags and goes into the hotel. She wants a hot shower and a long sleep after her trip.

items.prompt: Where does Mark come from?
items.audio:
Mark is a tourist from England. He is in the old part of the town of Khiva with a paper map in his hand, but he is lost. He sees a woman with a small dog and asks, Excuse me, can you help me? I want to go to the Juma Mosque. The woman, Gulnora, says, Of course. You are near it.

Go back to the main gate. Then take the first street on the right. Walk for five minutes past the souvenir shops. You will see a small fountain. Turn left at the fountain and the mosque is in front of you. It has many old wooden columns. Mark says, Is it open today? Gulnora says, Yes, but you must buy a ticket for ten thousand som.

Mark also asks about a good place for lunch. Gulnora says there is a nice café behind the mosque, and the soup is excellent there. She says, Do not go at noon, because it is full of tourists. Mark thanks her and takes a photo of her dog, whose name is Bobo. Then he walks away. After seven minutes he sees the fountain and the old columns. He smiles because he is not lost any more.

Mark is a tourist from England. He is in the old part of the town of Khiva with a paper map in his hand, but he is lost. He sees a woman with a small dog and asks, Excuse me, can you help me? I want to go to the Juma Mosque. The woman, Gulnora, says, Of course. You are near it.

Go back to the main gate. Then take the first street on the right. Walk for five minutes past the souvenir shops. You will see a small fountain. Turn left at the fountain and the mosque is in front of you. It has many old wooden columns. Mark says, Is it open today? Gulnora says, Yes, but you must buy a ticket for ten thousand som.

Mark also asks about a good place for lunch. Gulnora says there is a nice café behind the mosque, and the soup is excellent there. She says, Do not go at noon, because it is full of tourists. Mark thanks her and takes a photo of her dog, whose name is Bobo. Then he walks away. After seven minutes he sees the fountain and the old columns. He smiles because he is not lost any more.

Welcome to the city tour, everybody. My name is Sevara and I am your guide today. Our bus leaves from the hotel at nine thirty. The tour lasts three hours and we visit five places. Please stay with the group and look for my yellow flag. I hope you all enjoy this beautiful old city.

First we go to the Registan Square, with three beautiful old schools. They are more than five hundred years old. Then we drive to the big market and you have forty minutes for shopping. Next we see the famous tomb of a great king, called Timur. After that we have lunch in a garden restaurant. The restaurant is near a quiet river.

Please do not touch the old walls. You can take photos, but not inside the tomb. Water is on the bus and it is free. At the end of the tour, we come back to the hotel at half past twelve. If you have a question, please put up your hand. Does anybody have a question now? Good. Please get on the bus. Have a wonderful day and thank you for choosing our tour.

items.prompt: Where does Aziz fly to?
items.audio:
Aziz is at Tashkent airport. He flies to Istanbul and his plane leaves at two in the afternoon. He goes to the check-in desk at noon. The woman at the desk is called Malika. She says, Good afternoon. Passport and ticket, please. Aziz gives them to her.

Malika asks, Do you have any bags? Aziz says, I have one big suitcase and one small bag. She puts the suitcase on the scale. It weighs twenty-two kilos, and the limit is twenty-three kilos. So there is no problem. She says, Do you want a window seat or an aisle seat? Aziz says, A window seat, please. I love to look at the clouds.

Malika gives him a boarding pass. She says, Your gate is gate number nine. Boarding starts at one fifteen. You can wait in the café or visit the duty-free shop. Please be at the gate on time. Aziz thanks her. Then he goes through security and buys a bottle of water and a magazine. At the gate he sits and calls his mother to say goodbye. He is a little nervous, but he is also excited about the trip.

items.prompt: What is the name of the hotel?
items.audio:
Welcome to the Silk Road Hotel. My name is Laylo and I work at the reception desk. I want to tell you about our hotel. Reception is open all day and all night. You can ask us for help at any time. Your room is on the third floor. You can use the lift near the front door, or you can take the stairs.

Breakfast is from seven to ten in the restaurant on the first floor. It is free for all guests. We have bread, eggs, cheese, tea and fruit. Dinner is at seven in the evening, but you must pay for it. The swimming pool is on the roof and it is open from eight in the morning until eight at night. There is also wifi in every room. The password is on a small card in your room.

Check-out time is twelve noon. If you need to leave later, please tell us. You can leave your bags here for free. If you want a taxi, we can call one for you. A map of the city is on the table near the door. The post office is just across the street. Please do not make noise after eleven at night. We hope you enjoy your stay.

items.prompt: What is in the middle of the town?
items.audio:
Look at the map of our town. In the middle there is a big square with a fountain. On the north side of the square is the town hall. It is a grey building with a clock. On the south side there is a school and a small park. Many children play there after lessons.

The river is in the east. A long bridge goes over the river, and on the other side there is a football field. In the west, you can see the railway station and the bus station. They are near each other. The hospital is in the north-west, behind the station. The market is in the south-east, between the park and the river. It is open every day except Monday.

There are two main streets. Navoi Street goes from north to south, and Amir Temur Street goes from east to west. They cross in the square. The cinema is on the corner of these two streets. Next to the cinema there is a bakery, which sells hot bread in the morning. The mosque is behind the bakery. If you walk from the station to the river, it takes about twenty minutes.

At Pakhtakor you can change to the blue line. Please follow the blue signs. The train on the blue line comes every four minutes. Trains run from five in the morning until midnight. A single ticket costs one thousand four hundred som, and you can buy it from the machine at the entrance. Students pay half price.

Please stand behind the yellow line on the platform. Do not run on the stairs. Give your seat to old people, and to people with babies. Do not put your bags on the seats. If you lose something, please go to the office at the main station. We wish you a safe journey. The next station is Pakhtakor. Thank you for listening, and have a good day.

items.prompt: Where do the friends want to go?
items.audio:
Jasur and his friends have a plan for the weekend. They want to go to Lake Aydar. It is a big blue lake in the desert, about three hours from the city by car. Jasur's friend Timur has a car, so he is the driver. They meet at seven on Saturday morning in front of Jasur's house.

There are five people in the group: Jasur, Timur, Nodira, Olga and a boy called Sam. Nodira buys the food. She wants sandwiches, apples, and a lot of water. Olga brings a big tent, because they want to sleep near the lake. Sam brings a guitar. Jasur is in charge of the map. He says, The road goes through two small villages, and in the second village we stop for tea.

On Saturday they swim, play football on the sand and cook dinner on a fire. On Sunday they wake up early to see the sun come up over the lake. They go home at three in the afternoon because on Monday they have work. Jasur says, It will be a perfect weekend if it does not rain. The weather report says it will be sunny and warm.

Jasur and his friends have a plan for the weekend. They want to go to Lake Aydar. It is a big blue lake in the desert, about three hours from the city by car. Jasur's friend Timur has a car, so he is the driver. They meet at seven on Saturday morning in front of Jasur's house.

There are five people in the group: Jasur, Timur, Nodira, Olga and a boy called Sam. Nodira buys the food. She wants sandwiches, apples, and a lot of water. Olga brings a big tent, because they want to sleep near the lake. Sam brings a guitar. Jasur is in charge of the map. He says, The road goes through two small villages, and in the second village we stop for tea.

On Saturday they swim, play football on the sand and cook dinner on a fire. On Sunday they wake up early to see the sun come up over the lake. They go home at three in the afternoon because on Monday they have work. Jasur says, It will be a perfect weekend if it does not rain. The weather report says it will be sunny and warm.

items.prompt: Who is the postcard for?
items.audio:
Dear Grandma, greetings from Samarkand. I am writing this postcard in a small café near the Registan. The weather is hot and sunny, and I am drinking cold lemon tea. I arrived here on Tuesday by fast train. The trip from Tashkent took only two hours, and I sat next to a very nice old man.

My hotel is small but clean. My room has a balcony and I can see the blue domes from my window. Every morning I eat bread with honey and drink green tea. Yesterday I visited the big market and bought a colourful scarf for you. It is red and yellow, and I think you will love it. I also bought sweet dried fruit for Dad.

Tomorrow I am going to visit the observatory of Ulugbek. Then on Friday I take the train home. I miss you and the cat very much. Please give her a big kiss from me. I will tell you all about my trip when I come home. With love, your granddaughter, Zilola.

items.prompt: Who does Gulchehra send the parcel to?
items.audio:
It is Wednesday morning and Gulchehra goes to the post office on Mirzo Ulugbek Street. She wants to send a parcel to her brother in Russia. The post office opens at nine, but there are already ten people in front of her. She takes a number from the machine. She waits for fifteen minutes.

At last it is her turn. The clerk, a young man called Sherzod, says, How can I help you? Gulchehra says, I want to send this parcel to Moscow. It has a warm jacket and some books. Sherzod puts the parcel on the scale. It weighs three kilos. He says, It costs eighty thousand som and it takes seven days to arrive. Gulchehra says, That is fine. She also buys five stamps and two envelopes.

She writes her brother's address on a form with a blue pen. Sherzod gives her a receipt. He says, Keep it, so that you can check the parcel on the internet. Gulchehra pays with cash. When she goes out, she posts a letter for her aunt in the red box in front of the building. Then she walks to the bakery and buys two warm loaves of bread for lunch.

items.prompt: When do Hamid and Madina take a walk?
items.audio:
On Sunday morning, Hamid and his daughter Madina take a walk in the old town. The sun is warm and the streets are quiet. They start at the big gate and walk slowly. Madina is ten years old and she loves taking photographs. She has a new camera, a birthday present from her grandfather.

First they see a narrow street with old brown houses. Women sell colourful cloth and men sell clay pots in front of their doors. Hamid buys a small blue pot for his wife for five thousand som. Then they go to a tea house in a courtyard. They sit under a big tree. Hamid drinks black tea and Madina has a glass of orange juice and a piece of sweet cake.

After the tea house they visit the old school, called a madrasa. A guide tells them that students studied there six hundred years ago. Madina takes twenty photographs of the beautiful blue doors. At noon they climb the minaret, which has one hundred and twenty steps. From the top they can see the whole town. They are tired but happy. They walk home and show the photographs to Mum.

On Sunday morning, Hamid and his daughter Madina take a walk in the old town. The sun is warm and the streets are quiet. They start at the big gate and walk slowly. Madina is ten years old and she loves taking photographs. She has a new camera, a birthday present from her grandfather.

First they see a narrow street with old brown houses. Women sell colourful cloth and men sell clay pots in front of their doors. Hamid buys a small blue pot for his wife for five thousand som. Then they go to a tea house in a courtyard. They sit under a big tree. Hamid drinks black tea and Madina has a glass of orange juice and a piece of sweet cake.

After the tea house they visit the old school, called a madrasa. A guide tells them that students studied there six hundred years ago. Madina takes twenty photographs of the beautiful blue doors. At noon they climb the minaret, which has one hundred and twenty steps. From the top they can see the whole town. They are tired but happy. They walk home and show the photographs to Mum.

items.prompt: Which country does the writer visit?
items.audio:
Monday. Today is the first day of my trip to Kyrgyzstan. I woke up at five o'clock, because my bus left at six. It was a long ride, about nine hours, but the road through the mountains was very beautiful. I sat next to a girl called Aigul, who is a student of medicine. We talked about food and music. She gave me an apple, and I gave her a chocolate bar. We arrived in Bishkek at three in the afternoon.

Tuesday. Today I visited the main square. It is huge, and there are many pigeons. In the afternoon I took a taxi to the mountains. The driver, an old man called Bakyt, played traditional songs on his radio. We stopped at a small village and I drank fresh milk from a cow. It was the best milk of my life! The nights here are cold, so I wear a thick sweater.

Wednesday. Tomorrow I will go to a very big lake called Issyk-Kul. I plan to stay there for three days and sleep in a small wooden house. I will swim, ride a horse and write more in this diary. I miss my family, so I will call them tonight. Goodnight.

items.prompt: Who is giving the announcements?
items.audio:
Good morning, students. This is Mrs Karimova with the school announcements. Please listen carefully. Today is Monday, and lessons begin at eight thirty. The first lesson for every class is maths. Please go to your classroom quickly and quietly.

There is some good news this week. The school choir will sing in the main hall on Wednesday at two o'clock. Everyone can come and listen. Mr Brown, our music teacher, says the choir has practised for six weeks. The children are very ready, and they are a little excited.

There are also two small changes today. The library is closed this morning because workers are painting the walls. It will open again after lunch. The canteen has a new menu, too. Today there is chicken soup, rice and fruit. A bottle of water costs two hundred som, and a cup of tea costs one hundred som.

Finally, a reminder about lost things. A blue jacket and a black bag are in the office. If they are yours, please ask Mr Aziz at the front desk. He is there until four o'clock every day.

Thank you for listening. Have a wonderful day, and please remember to be kind to each other.

items.prompt: Who is speaking?
items.audio:
Welcome back, everyone. My name is Mr Yusupov, and I am the head teacher of this school. It is the first day of the new year, and I am very happy to see you all.

Our school has four hundred students and thirty teachers. This year we have some new things. We have a new sports hall, and we have twenty new computers in the computer room. We also have two new teachers. Miss Lola will teach English, and Mr Daniel will teach science.

Now let me talk about our rules. They are simple. First, please come to school on time. The bell rings at eight fifteen. Second, wear your school uniform every day. Third, do your homework and bring your books. Fourth, be polite to teachers and to your friends. If you have a problem, you can always come to my office.

I also have a big goal for this year. I want every student to read ten books. The library will help you choose them. At the end of the year, the best readers will get a small prize.

Students, learning is a long road, but you are not alone. Teachers, parents and friends are with you. Let us make this a great year. Thank you, and good luck.

items.prompt: What time does Aziza get up?
items.audio:
My name is Aziza, and I am eleven years old. I want to tell you about my day. I get up at six thirty every morning. First I wash my face and brush my teeth. Then I have breakfast with my family. I usually eat bread, an egg and a cup of tea.

I leave home at seven thirty. My school is not far, so I walk with my friend Malika. It takes fifteen minutes. Lessons start at eight and finish at two. I have six lessons every day. My favourite lesson is art because I love to draw.

After school I go home and have lunch. My mother cooks soup or rice. Then I rest for half an hour. At three thirty I do my homework. It takes about one hour. After that, I play with my little brother in the garden. He is five years old, and he likes football.

In the evening we have dinner at seven o'clock. My father comes home from work, and we all sit together. After dinner I help my mother wash the plates. Then I read a book or watch a short film.

I go to bed at nine thirty. Before I sleep, I say good night to my parents. I like my day because it is busy and happy.

items.prompt: On which days is there school?
items.audio:
Today I will explain our class timetable. Please look at your paper and listen carefully. We have school from Monday to Friday. There is no school on Saturday or Sunday.

On Monday, we start with English at eight o'clock. After that we have maths at nine. At ten we have a short break for twenty minutes. Then we study history. On Tuesday, the first lesson is science. Today it is in the laboratory, not in our classroom. Please do not go to room five by mistake.

Wednesday is the busiest day. We have five lessons, and the last one is sport. Please bring your sports shoes and a bottle of water. On Thursday we have art and music. Many students like Thursday because there is no homework in those lessons.

Friday is a short day. We have only four lessons, and school finishes at twelve thirty. In the last lesson, the teacher reads a story, and we can relax.

Lunch is at one o'clock on most days. Remember, the lunch break is forty minutes long. Please write the timetable in your notebook. Put a copy at home, too. If you forget it, you can ask me or a friend. Are there any questions? Good. Let us begin our first lesson.

items.prompt: When does Bobur come home?
items.audio:
Bobur comes home from school at three o'clock. His mother, Nilufar, is in the kitchen. She asks him, "How was school today?" Bobur answers, "It was good, Mum, but I have a lot of homework."

Nilufar asks him to tell her about it. Bobur says he has three tasks. First, he must write five sentences in English about his family. Second, he must do ten maths problems. Third, he must learn a poem for Friday. The poem has eight lines.

items.prompt: When do the exams begin?
items.audio:
Attention, please. This is an important notice about the end of year exams. Please listen to all the details, and write them down.

The exams begin on the third of June and finish on the tenth of June. There are five exams. The first is English on Monday. The second is maths on Tuesday. Science is on Thursday, history is on Friday, and the last exam is geography on the following Tuesday. Each exam starts at nine o'clock in the morning.

All exams take place in the main hall, not in your classrooms. Please arrive at eight forty so that you have time to find your seat. Students who arrive late cannot enter after nine fifteen.

Please bring two blue pens, a pencil, a ruler and a bottle of water. You cannot use a phone, a calculator or a dictionary in the hall. Please leave your bags outside.

The maths and science exams are one hour and thirty minutes long. The other exams are one hour. If you are ill on the day of an exam, ask a parent to call the school office as early as possible.

Finally, relax and sleep well the night before. You are ready. The teachers believe in you. Good luck, everyone.

items.prompt: Who is the speaker?
items.audio:
Welcome to our school library, new students. My name is Mrs Sultanova, and I am the librarian. Today I will show you around, and then you can get your own library card.

The library is open from eight in the morning until five in the afternoon. It is closed on Sundays. Please enter through the blue door on your left. We keep this room quiet, so please speak softly.

On the right you can see the story books. There are more than three thousand of them. The books for young readers have a green sticker. On the left are the books about science, animals and sport. The big table in the middle is for reading and homework. Six students can sit there together.

Behind me there are eight computers. You can use them to search for information or to write your homework. Each student can use a computer for thirty minutes. Please do not eat or drink in this room.

You can borrow three books at one time. You must bring them back after two weeks. If you need more time, just tell me. If you lose a book, please tell me at once, and we will find a way to help.

Now, who would like a library card first? Please make a line by the desk. Thank you.

Next is the long jump. Jasur from class six jumps three metres. That is a very good jump. Then Emma tries and jumps two metres and eighty centimetres. Jasur is the winner so far.

Now it is time for the team race. Each team has four runners, and they pass a small stick to each other. The blue team is quick, but the yellow team drops the stick. Oh no. The blue team wins easily, and the crowd is loud.

The prizes are ready, and there is cold water for everyone. Thank you for coming. It was a fantastic day.

items.prompt: What does Ms Green teach?
items.audio:
Ms Green is an English teacher. Every evening she makes a plan for the next day. Tonight she is planning a lesson for her class of twenty-two students. The lesson is about food, and it lasts forty-five minutes.

First, she wants a warm-up. For five minutes, the students will say the names of fruit and vegetables. They will stand up and call out words, one by one. Ms Green thinks this wakes them up.

Second, she will show ten pictures on the board. The pictures show bread, cheese, milk, eggs, rice and other things. She will say each word, and the students will repeat it. This takes ten minutes.

Third, there is a listening task. The students will hear a short talk about a boy at the market. They must write down what he buys. It will play twice. Then they will check their answers with a partner.

Fourth, the class will play a game. Students will work in groups of four. Each group makes a menu for a small cafe. They will draw it on a big piece of paper. The best menu wins a sticker.

At the end, Ms Green will give them a short homework task. They must write three sentences about their favourite food. She puts her notes in a blue folder and goes home happy.

items.prompt: What time does the alarm ring?
items.audio:
Jasur is a student in class seven. His mornings are always very busy. Today his alarm clock rings at six forty-five, but he does not want to get up. He turns it off and sleeps for five more minutes. Then his mother opens the door and says, "Jasur, it is late."

He jumps out of bed, washes his face and puts on his school uniform. He cannot find his left sock. He looks under the bed, and there it is. His sister laughs at him.

At the table, there is hot porridge and a glass of milk. Jasur eats quickly because he does not want to miss the bus. His mother puts an apple and a small sandwich in his bag for lunch.

At seven twenty he runs to the bus stop. The bus usually comes at seven thirty. Today it is five minutes late, so he has time to breathe. His friend Ali is already there. They talk about the football match from last night.

The bus ride takes twenty minutes. When Jasur arrives at school, he remembers something terrible. His maths book is on the kitchen table. He is sad, but Ali says, "Do not worry. You can share my book today." Jasur smiles and says thank you.

Jasur is a student in class seven. His mornings are always very busy. Today his alarm clock rings at six forty-five, but he does not want to get up. He turns it off and sleeps for five more minutes. Then his mother opens the door and says, "Jasur, it is late."

He jumps out of bed, washes his face and puts on his school uniform. He cannot find his left sock. He looks under the bed, and there it is. His sister laughs at him.

At the table, there is hot porridge and a glass of milk. Jasur eats quickly because he does not want to miss the bus. His mother puts an apple and a small sandwich in his bag for lunch.

At seven twenty he runs to the bus stop. The bus usually comes at seven thirty. Today it is five minutes late, so he has time to breathe. His friend Ali is already there. They talk about the football match from last night.

The bus ride takes twenty minutes. When Jasur arrives at school, he remembers something terrible. His maths book is on the kitchen table. He is sad, but Ali says, "Do not worry. You can share my book today." Jasur smiles and says thank you.

items.prompt: Who is speaking about the clubs?
items.audio:
Hello, new students. I am Mr Anvar, and I will tell you about our after-school clubs. Every club is free, and everyone is welcome. Please choose one or two clubs that you like.

On Monday, there is the chess club. It starts at three thirty in room nine. Beginners learn simple moves, and older players have small games. On Tuesday, we have the drama club. They are making a short play about a lost dog. They need actors, and they also need students to make costumes.

On Wednesday, the football club meets on the school field at four o'clock. Please bring your sports shoes. The coach is Mr Aziz, and he is very friendly. On Thursday, there is the art club in room fourteen. Students paint, draw and make small models from paper.

On Friday, the reading club meets in the library at three o'clock. The members read one book each month and talk about it. This month the book is a funny story about a talking cat.

All clubs finish at five o'clock. Parents can come and take the children home at that time. If you want to join, please write your name on the list outside my office. The list closes on the end of this week. I hope to see you all soon.

items.prompt: Who is the teacher calling?
items.audio:
Mrs Yusupova is a teacher at a primary school. This evening she is calling the mother of one of her students. The student is a nine-year-old girl called Sevara. The mother's name is Gulnora.

Mrs Yusupova says, "Good evening, Mrs Gulnora. I have good news about Sevara." The mother is happy. The teacher says that Sevara is a kind and clever girl. She helps her friends and always listens in class. Her reading is excellent this term.

Then the teacher says there is one small problem. Sevara often forgets her homework notebook. Last week she forgot it three times. Mrs Gulnora is surprised and says she will check the bag every night. The teacher thanks her and says that a small habit can solve the problem.

Mrs Yusupova also says that Sevara is a little shy in maths lessons. She does not like to answer in front of the class. The teacher suggests that Sevara practise at home. Ten minutes a day is enough. She can use number cards or a simple game.

Finally, the teacher invites the mother to a meeting on Thursday at four o'clock. They will talk about the end of term. Mrs Gulnora says she will come. Both women say goodbye, and the call ends. It lasted about eight minutes.

items.prompt: What time does the lunch break start?
items.audio:
It is twelve thirty, and the lunch break has started. Nodira and her friend Kate are in the school canteen. They are looking for a table. The room is noisy, and there are many children in line.

Nodira asks Kate, "What would you like to eat today?" Kate says she wants pasta with tomato sauce and a glass of apple juice. Nodira takes a plate of rice with chicken and a salad. The lady at the counter smiles and gives them each a small piece of cake. She says it is for the birthday of the cook.

Good morning, class seven. I am Mr Davron, and I want to tell you about next week's school trip. We are going to the National Museum in the city. It is an exciting day, so please listen to the plan.

We will meet at the school gate on Friday at seven forty-five. Please do not be late, because the bus leaves at eight o'clock exactly. The ride takes one hour. Please sit down and keep your seat belt on.

At the museum we will see old coins, clay pots and large maps. A guide called Miss Lena will show us around. The tour takes ninety minutes. You can ask her questions, but please do not touch anything. After the tour, we will have lunch in the museum garden. Please bring your own sandwich and a bottle of water. There is a small shop, but it is expensive.

Please wear comfortable shoes and a warm jacket. The weather will be cool. Bring a pen and a small notebook, too. After the visit, each student must write five sentences about their favourite thing.

We will come back to school at three o'clock. If you want to go, please give this paper to your parents. They must sign it and return it to me by Wednesday. Thank you, and I hope you enjoy the trip.

items.prompt: How old is Timur?
items.audio:
My name is Timur, and I am twelve years old. My weekdays are busy, but my weekends are slow and relaxed. I want to tell you what I usually do on Saturday and Sunday.

On Saturday I get up late, at nine o'clock. My mother makes pancakes, and we eat them with honey. After breakfast I clean my room and help my father in the garden. We water the flowers and pick some tomatoes. It takes about an hour.

In the afternoon I meet my friends at the park. We play football for two hours. Sometimes my cousin Anna comes with us, and she is a very good player. When we are tired, we sit under a tree and drink cold lemonade. At six o'clock I go home, take a shower and have dinner.

On Sunday I get up early, at eight, because we visit my grandparents. They live in a small house ten minutes away. My grandmother cooks a big lunch, and my grandfather tells old stories. I love his stories about the mountains.

In the evening, I pack my school bag for Monday and check my timetable. I read a book for half an hour and go to bed at nine thirty. A good weekend makes me ready for the new week.

items.prompt: What kind of animal is Snow?
items.audio:
My name is Aziza and I want to talk about my pet. His name is Snow. He is a small white rabbit. I got him two years ago on my birthday. My uncle gave him to me. At first Snow was shy and hid under the sofa, but now he is very friendly.

Snow lives in a big cage in my bedroom. Every morning I give him fresh water and some food. He eats carrots, grass and a little lettuce. His favourite food is the green leaves of a carrot. He does not like apples. I clean his cage every Saturday with my father.

Snow is very quiet, but he can jump very high. In the afternoon I let him run in the garden. He jumps and plays for about an hour. My little brother Timur likes to watch him. Sometimes Snow sleeps on my feet when I read a book.

I take Snow to the doctor twice a year. The doctor, Mrs Karimova, says he is healthy. He weighs two kilos. I love my rabbit very much. A pet is a lot of work, but it is also a lot of fun. Do you have a pet at home?

items.prompt: Who is the swimming teacher?
items.audio:
Today is Tuesday, and it is time for the swimming lesson. Eight children stand by the pool. The teacher is Coach Olga. She is kind and she always smiles. The water is warm, and the pool is twenty-five metres long.

First, the children put on their caps and goggles. Coach Olga says, you must not run near the pool. It is dangerous. Then they sit on the edge and put their feet in the water. A boy called Jasur is afraid of the deep water. Coach Olga holds his hand and says, do not worry.

Now the children practise their legs. Each child holds a blue board and kicks fast. After ten minutes they learn to move their arms. A girl named Madina swims the best. She can swim across the pool in only forty seconds. The others clap for her.

At the end of the lesson there is a game. The children pick up yellow rings from the bottom of the pool. Jasur finds three rings and is very proud. The lesson finishes at six o'clock. The children take a warm shower, get dressed and go home. Their parents wait for them outside with towels and fruit.

items.prompt: When does the zoo close?
items.audio:
Welcome to the city zoo, my friends. My name is Rustam and I am your guide today. The zoo opens at nine o'clock and closes at five. We have more than two hundred animals here. Please stay with the group and do not feed the animals.

Our first stop is the elephants. We have three elephants. The biggest one is called Gulya. She is thirty years old and she eats about one hundred kilos of food every day. Elephants also love to play in the water.

Next, look at the monkeys on the left. They are very clever and funny. They climb trees and make noises all day. Be careful with your bags because monkeys like to take things.

Now we walk to the lions. The male lion sleeps for almost twenty hours a day. In the evening he wakes up and walks around. Lions are quiet in the afternoon, so we are lucky if we hear one roar.

Finally, we visit the penguins. They live in a cold house with ice. The keeper feeds them fish at two o'clock. Come and watch! After that, you can have lunch in the cafe near the gate or buy a small toy in the shop. Enjoy your day!

items.prompt: What time does the class begin?
items.audio:
Every Saturday morning I go to a dance class. The class is in the old community centre near my house. It begins at ten o'clock and finishes at eleven thirty. My teacher is Miss Laura. She comes from Spain, and she teaches us salsa.

There are twelve students in my class. Most of them are young women, but there are also three men. My best friend Zarina comes with me. We pay twenty dollars for four lessons. It is not expensive.

First, we warm up for ten minutes. We stretch our arms and legs and move to slow music. Then Miss Laura shows us a new step. Salsa has a simple rhythm: one, two, three, pause. At first I often stood on my partner's feet! Now I am much better.

After the steps, we dance with a partner. We change partners every five minutes, so we can meet everybody. The music is fast and happy, and everybody laughs. Miss Laura says that dancing is good for your heart and your mind.

Next month we have a show. We will dance on the stage in front of our families. I am a little nervous, but I am also excited. I will wear a long red dress.

items.prompt: Who taught Mr Ismoil to play chess?
items.audio:
Hello, young players, and welcome to our school chess club. My name is Mr Ismoil. I started playing chess when I was six years old. My grandfather taught me. He always said that chess makes you patient.

Our club meets every Wednesday after school. We play in room fourteen, next to the library. There are twenty members now. Last year there were only eight. The club is free, and beginners are very welcome.

Let me explain the board. It has sixty-four squares, half black and half white. Each player has sixteen pieces. The most important piece is the king, but the queen is the strongest. The pawns are small and slow, but they can become queens at the end of the board.

In the first month you will learn how the pieces move. Then we will play short games with a clock. Each player has ten minutes. Do not worry if you lose. Everybody loses games, even the best players. Losing helps you learn.

In May we have a school tournament. The winner gets a silver cup and a new chess book. Last year the winner was a girl called Sevara. She was only eleven years old. Maybe this year you will win!

items.prompt: What time did they wake up?
items.audio:
Last summer I went fishing with my grandfather. His name is Karim, and he loves fishing more than anything. We woke up very early, at four o'clock, when it was still dark. Grandmother made us tea and four sandwiches with cheese.

We drove to a small lake in the mountains. It took one hour. The air was cold and the water was very quiet. Grandfather gave me a short red fishing rod. He showed me how to put a worm on the hook.

For two hours I caught nothing. I was bored and a little cold. Grandfather said, be patient, Ali. Fish are not in a hurry. Then suddenly my rod moved. I pulled hard and I saw a big silver fish. It was a trout, and it weighed two kilos. I was so happy that I shouted.

Grandfather caught three small fish, but mine was the biggest. We did not keep the small ones. We put them back in the water. We ate our sandwiches near a big tree, and a duck came to look at us.

In the evening we cooked my trout on a fire. It was delicious. I will never forget that day. Next summer I want to go again.

items.prompt: On which floor does the family live?
items.audio:
Mimi is a small grey cat. She lives with the Rahimov family in a flat on the third floor. Her day is very busy, even if she sleeps a lot.

At six o'clock in the morning Mimi wakes up. She is hungry, so she walks to Mrs Rahimova's bed and says meow. Mrs Rahimova gets up and puts fish and milk in her bowl. Mimi eats everything in two minutes.

After breakfast, Mimi sits on the window sill. She watches the birds in the tree. Her tail moves from side to side. She would like to catch a bird, but the window is closed. At ten o'clock she sleeps on the sofa until lunch.

In the afternoon the children come home from school. The youngest, a boy named Sardor, plays with Mimi. He pulls a long string, and Mimi jumps and runs after it. She is very fast. Her favourite toy is a small blue ball with a bell inside.

In the evening the family watches television. Mimi sits on the knees of Mr Rahimov. He gently touches her head, and she makes a soft sound. At ten o'clock everybody goes to bed. Mimi sleeps on a warm blanket at the end of the bed. Tomorrow will be the same, and Mimi is happy.

items.prompt: How long has Nargiza's family lived on the farm?
items.audio:
Hello, children, and welcome to my farm. My name is Nargiza, and I am a farmer. My family has lived here for fifty years. Today I will show you around. Please walk slowly and listen to me.

First, we visit the cows. We have fifteen cows, and they give us milk every morning and evening. The oldest cow is called Oq. Each cow drinks about fifty litres of water a day. You can touch her, but be gentle.

Next to the cows is the chicken house. We have about sixty chickens. Every morning the children of the farm collect the eggs. You can help us today! Put the eggs carefully in the basket.

Behind the chickens there are four sheep and two horses. The horses are brown and very strong. My son Davron rides his horse to the field every day. If you want, you can ride a small horse for five minutes.

Finally, we go to the vegetable garden. We grow tomatoes, onions and potatoes. In autumn we sell them at the market on Sundays. After the tour, we will eat fresh bread with honey and drink warm milk in the yard. I hope you enjoy your visit!

items.prompt: On which days are the lessons?
items.audio:
Last month I started guitar lessons. My teacher is Mr Anvar, and he is a very patient man. The lessons are on Mondays and Thursdays at five o'clock. Each lesson is forty-five minutes long. I walk to his small studio, which is above a bakery. It always smells of fresh bread there!

My guitar is old, but it has a beautiful sound. It was my cousin's guitar. It has six strings. In my first lesson, Mr Anvar showed me the names of the strings. Then he taught me three easy notes. My fingers hurt a lot!

Now I can play a short song called Happy Birthday. I practise at home every day for half an hour. My mother says the sound is terrible, but my little sister likes it. She sings with me. Mr Anvar says practice is more important than talent. He says it is better to play ten minutes every day than two hours once a week.

Next week he will teach me a famous folk song. I want to play it for my grandmother on her birthday in December. She loves music. I think she will cry because she will be so happy.

items.prompt: How far is the lake?
items.audio:
This Saturday my friends and I want to go on a long cycling trip. There are four of us: me, Farhod, Lena and her brother Max. We plan to ride to the lake near the old castle. The lake is thirty kilometres from our town.

We will meet at seven o'clock in front of the school. It is better to start early because the day will be hot. Farhod will bring a small pump and some tools in case of a problem. Lena will bring the map. Max is the youngest, so we will ride slowly for him.

The road goes along a river and through a quiet forest. There are only a few cars. We will stop after fifteen kilometres to drink water and eat bananas. Everybody must wear a helmet. It is the rule of our group.

At the lake we will have a picnic. I will make cheese sandwiches, and Lena will bring apple juice. After lunch we can swim for one hour, if the weather is good. The weather report says it will be sunny, with no rain.

We want to ride home at three o'clock. We should arrive about six in the evening. I am very excited, and I have already checked my bike. The brakes are good, and the tyres are full.

items.prompt: How old was Dilnoza when she started painting?
items.audio:
Good evening, and thank you for coming to my exhibition. My name is Dilnoza, and I am a painter. I started painting when I was nine years old. My first picture was a red apple on a blue table. My mother still keeps it in her kitchen.

Today you can see thirty paintings on these walls. Most of them show mountains, rivers and old houses from my home village. I love nature, so I paint outside whenever the weather is nice. I get up early, at five o'clock, because the morning light is soft and beautiful.

My favourite colour is yellow. It makes me feel warm and happy. Some people think my pictures are too bright, but I like bright colours. This big painting near the door is called Autumn Market. It took me three months to finish. It shows women who sell pumpkins and bread.

I also teach children to paint on Fridays in the town library. Children are not afraid of colours, and I learn a lot from them. If you want to buy a picture, the prices are on the small white cards. The cheapest costs fifty dollars. The exhibition is open until the end of the month. Please enjoy the paintings and have some tea!

Good evening, and thank you for coming to my exhibition. My name is Dilnoza, and I am a painter. I started painting when I was nine years old. My first picture was a red apple on a blue table. My mother still keeps it in her kitchen.

Today you can see thirty paintings on these walls. Most of them show mountains, rivers and old houses from my home village. I love nature, so I paint outside whenever the weather is nice. I get up early, at five o'clock, because the morning light is soft and beautiful.

My favourite colour is yellow. It makes me feel warm and happy. Some people think my pictures are too bright, but I like bright colours. This big painting near the door is called Autumn Market. It took me three months to finish. It shows women who sell pumpkins and bread.

I also teach children to paint on Fridays in the town library. Children are not afraid of colours, and I learn a lot from them. If you want to buy a picture, the prices are on the small white cards. The cheapest costs fifty dollars. The exhibition is open until the end of the month. Please enjoy the paintings and have some tea!

It is a warm Sunday, and the final of the town tennis cup begins. Two players stand on the court: Kamila and Elena. Kamila is seventeen years old, and she plays with her left hand. Elena is older, twenty-two, and she is the champion of last year.

The match starts at two o'clock. Elena serves first. Her serve is very fast, and Kamila misses the first ball. Elena wins the first game. But Kamila does not give up. She runs to every ball and hits it back hard. She wins the second game and the third.

The crowd is excited. About two hundred people sit around the court. A small boy shouts, go, Kamila! The sun is hot, and the players drink water every few minutes. The umpire sits on a high chair and says the score in a loud voice.

After one hour Kamila wins the first set, six games to four. In the second set Elena becomes tired. She makes many mistakes and hits the ball into the net. Kamila wins the second set six games to two.

The match ends at four o'clock. Kamila jumps with joy, and then she shakes hands with Elena. Her coach hugs her. The prize is a silver cup and one thousand dollars. It is a great day for the young player.

items.prompt: What time does Jamshid start work?
items.audio:
My name is Jamshid, and I am a dog walker. I walk other people's dogs when the owners are at work. I love my job because I love animals, and I can be outside all day.

Every morning I start at eight o'clock. First, I visit a small white dog named Bella. She lives in a flat near the bus station. Bella is old, so we walk slowly for twenty minutes. Then I pick up two brothers, Max and Rocky. They are young black dogs with a lot of energy. We go to the big park and they run after a ball for an hour.

At noon I give water to the dogs and eat my own lunch on a bench. Many people stop and say hello to the dogs. Children love Rocky because he has one brown ear and one black ear.

In the afternoon I take a big dog called Tiger to the river. He loves swimming, and he always shakes water on me! I carry a bag with towels, snacks and a small bottle of water.

I earn ten dollars for each walk. It is not a lot, but I walk six dogs a day. The best part of the job is the way the dogs look at me when I arrive. Their tails move happily.

items.prompt: What time does the family leave home?
items.audio:
On Sunday our family always goes to the city park. It is our favourite day of the week. The park is big and green, and it has a small lake in the middle. We leave home at ten o'clock and walk for fifteen minutes.

My father likes to play football with my brother Sanjar. They play near the old oak tree. My mother usually reads a book on a bench under the trees. I like to ride my scooter on the long path around the lake. It is smooth and has no cars.

Near the lake there is a playground. Many small children play on the swings and the slide. A man sells ice cream next to the gate. A big ice cream costs two dollars, and my favourite flavour is strawberry. I always ask my father for one at noon.
