items.prompt: How long did Aziz stay in the village?
items.audio:
Last summer Aziz spent three weeks in his grandparents' village near Fergana. He went there by bus with his mother on the first of July. The ride was long, about six hours, but he listened to music and looked at the fields.

His grandfather, Rustam, was at the bus stop. He was very happy to see Aziz. The house was big and had a green gate. In the garden there were apple trees and a small pond with ducks. Every morning Aziz got up at six o'clock and helped his grandmother. She gave him warm bread and milk for breakfast.

After breakfast Aziz and his cousin Bobur went to the river. They swam, played football on the grass and caught small fish. Aziz was not good at fishing, but Bobur taught him. On the second Sunday they picked cherries with grandfather. They filled two big baskets and made jam in the evening.

In the evenings the family sat outside and drank tea. Grandfather told old stories about the village. Aziz liked this part of the day best, because the air was cool and the sky was full of stars.

On the last day Aziz felt sad. Grandmother gave him a jar of cherry jam for his mother. He promised to come back next summer and bring his sister Laylo too.

Last summer Aziz spent three weeks in his grandparents' village near Fergana. He went there by bus with his mother on the first of July. The ride was long, about six hours, but he listened to music and looked at the fields.

His grandfather, Rustam, was at the bus stop. He was very happy to see Aziz. The house was big and had a green gate. In the garden there were apple trees and a small pond with ducks. Every morning Aziz got up at six o'clock and helped his grandmother. She gave him warm bread and milk for breakfast.

After breakfast Aziz and his cousin Bobur went to the river. They swam, played football on the grass and caught small fish. Aziz was not good at fishing, but Bobur taught him. On the second Sunday they picked cherries with grandfather. They filled two big baskets and made jam in the evening.

In the evenings the family sat outside and drank tea. Grandfather told old stories about the village. Aziz liked this part of the day best, because the air was cool and the sky was full of stars.

On the last day Aziz felt sad. Grandmother gave him a jar of cherry jam for his mother. He promised to come back next summer and bring his sister Laylo too.
items.explain: He was not good at fishing.

items.prompt: How deep was the snow in the morning?
items.audio:
This morning Madina woke up and the world was white. It snowed all night, and now the snow was almost thirty centimetres deep. She ran to the window and shouted, "Mum, look! Snow!" Her little brother Jasur jumped out of bed and ran to the window too.

School was closed because the roads were icy. The children were very happy. Mum made hot chocolate, and they put on warm coats, hats, gloves and big boots. Madina also wore a red scarf, her favourite one.

Outside, the street was quiet and beautiful. Their neighbour, Mister Karim, was already clearing snow from his car. The children built a snowman in front of the house. It had two stones for eyes and a carrot for a nose. Jasur gave it his old blue hat. Then they made snowballs and played with their friends Dina and Timur for an hour.

After that Madina's hands were cold and her nose was red. They went inside and sat near the heater. Mum gave them soup and warm bread. In the afternoon they drew pictures of the snowman and watched a film.

In the evening the snow started again. Madina smiled. She hoped it was going to snow tomorrow too, because she wanted another day without school.

items.prompt: On which floor is the flat?
items.audio:
Hello, Sardor. Welcome to my new flat! Come in, and I will show you everything. We live on the fourth floor, and there is a lift, so it is easy to carry heavy bags.

This is the hall. Here you can leave your shoes and your coat. On the left is the kitchen. It is small, but it is bright and clean. We have a new fridge, a cooker and a table for four people. My mother cooks here every evening.

Next, this is the living room. It is the biggest room in the flat. There is a grey sofa, a television and a bookshelf with my father's old books. The windows are big, and in the afternoon the sun comes in. Behind the sofa there is a balcony. We have two chairs there, and my mother grows flowers in pots.

On the right there are two bedrooms. The first one is for my parents. The second one is mine, and I share it with my brother Anvar. We have a bunk bed. I sleep on the top, and he sleeps on the bottom. The bathroom is between the bedrooms, and it has a small window.

The flat has three rooms and costs a lot of money, but we like it. It is close to my school, and the park is only five minutes away. Now, please sit down. Would you like some tea?

items.prompt: What colour are the walls?
items.audio:
My name is Gulnora, and I want to tell you about my room. It is my favourite place in our house. It is not very big, but it is warm and quiet. The walls are light yellow, and the curtains are white with small blue flowers.

When you open the door, you can see my bed on the right. It has a soft pink blanket and three pillows. Next to the bed there is a small table with a lamp. I read there every night before I sleep. Above the bed there are four photos of my family and my best friend Zarina.

On the left there is a big wardrobe for my clothes. It is brown and very old, but I love it. Near the window there is my desk. I do my homework there. On the desk there are a laptop, a green notebook and a cup with pens. The window looks at our garden, and in spring I can see the apple trees in flower.

There is also a round carpet on the floor. It is grey, and it is very soft. My cat, Mushuk, likes to sleep on it. Sometimes she jumps on the desk, and then I cannot work!

I clean my room every Saturday. My mother says it is the tidiest room in the house, and I am proud of that. Every evening I turn on the lamp, close the curtains and feel happy.

When you open the door, you can see my bed on the right. It has a soft pink blanket and three pillows. Next to the bed there is a small table with a lamp. I read there every night before I sleep. Above the bed there are four photos of my family and my best friend Zarina.

On the left there is a big wardrobe for my clothes. It is brown and very old, but I love it. Near the window there is my desk. I do my homework there. On the desk there are a laptop, a green notebook and a cup with pens. The window looks at our garden, and in spring I can see the apple trees in flower.

There is also a round carpet on the floor. It is grey, and it is very soft. My cat, Mushuk, likes to sleep on it. Sometimes she jumps on the desk, and then I cannot work!

I clean my room every Saturday. My mother says it is the tidiest room in the house, and I am proud of that. Every evening I turn on the lamp, close the curtains and feel happy.

items.prompt: When do the speaker and her father buy the tree?
items.audio:
Hello, class. Today I want to tell you about our plan for New Year. My family loves this holiday, and we always get ready for it early.

On the twenty-eighth of December my father and I are going to buy a New Year tree. We want a green tree about two metres tall. My mother is going to buy lights and small toys for it. Then my sister Nigora and I will put everything on the tree. It takes about an hour, and we listen to music at the same time.

On the thirtieth of December my mother and my grandmother are going to cook. They make plov, a big salad and a cake with nuts. I always help with the salad. I wash the vegetables, and my grandmother cuts them.

On the thirty-first of December our relatives come at seven o'clock in the evening. There are ten people, and the table is full of food. We watch a concert on television and wait for midnight. At twelve o'clock we say, "Happy New Year!" and give each other presents. This year I am going to give my father a warm scarf.

After midnight we go outside and look at the fireworks. The next day we sleep late, and in the afternoon we visit our neighbours. I think it will be a wonderful holiday.

items.prompt: Where did the friends go camping?
items.audio:
Last weekend my friends and I went camping in the mountains near Chimgan. There were five of us: me, my brother Otabek, and our friends Kamila, Dmitry and Zafar. We left the city at eight o'clock in the morning and arrived at eleven.

First we put up two tents next to a small river. The place was beautiful, with tall trees and green grass. Kamila and Dmitry collected wood, and Zafar made a fire. In the afternoon we walked up a hill and took many photos. The view was amazing.

At six o'clock we cooked dinner on the fire. We had sausages, potatoes and tea. Everything tasted very good because we were hungry. After dinner it got cold, so we put on our jackets and sat near the fire.

Otabek played the guitar, and we sang songs. Later Dmitry told a funny story about a bear, and we laughed a lot. Then we looked at the sky. There were thousands of stars, and we saw one shooting star. Kamila made a wish, but she did not tell us.

At eleven o'clock we went to sleep. In the night it rained a little, and the tents were wet in the morning. We did not mind. We had breakfast, cleaned the place and took all our rubbish home. It was the best weekend of the summer.

items.prompt: When does Navruz come?
items.audio:
Navruz is my favourite holiday. It comes on the twenty-first of March, when spring begins. This year our family had a big party in our yard, and I want to tell you about it.

The day before, my mother and my aunts cooked sumalak. It is a sweet dish made from wheat, and it takes a whole night to cook. The women sang songs and took turns to stir it. In the morning the smell was wonderful. We also had samsa, plov, and a lot of fruit and sweets.

At ten o'clock the guests arrived. My uncle Habib came with his three children, and our neighbours Mister and Missus Rahimov came with a big cake. The yard was full of people. My grandfather wore his best coat and a colourful cap. Children had new clothes, and the girls had flowers in their hair.

After lunch there were games. We ran in bags, jumped over a small fire and played a game with eggs. My cousin Sevara won the race, and she got a small prize. Then a man played the doira, and everyone danced. I danced with my little sister for a long time.

The party finished at six o'clock. I was tired, but I felt very happy. In the evening we cleaned the yard and watched the sunset together.

items.prompt: How long will the cleaning take?
items.audio:
It is Saturday morning, and Mother is not happy. The house is very untidy. She calls her children, Bekzod and Malika, and says, "Today we clean the whole house together. It will take about three hours."

Bekzod asks, "Do I have to do it, Mum? I want to play football with my friends." Mother answers, "You can play in the afternoon. First, please clean your room. Put your toys in the box and make your bed." Bekzod sighs, but he goes to his room.

Malika asks, "What can I do?" Mother says, "You can wash the dishes and wipe the kitchen table. Then please sweep the floor in the hall." Malika takes a cloth and starts to work. She likes the kitchen, because the radio is there, and she listens to songs.

Mother cleans the bathroom and washes the windows. She opens them to let in fresh air. Father comes home from the shop with a new mop and a bag of washing powder. He helps with the big carpet in the living room. Together they take it outside and shake it.

At twelve o'clock the house is clean and smells of lemon. Everybody is tired and hungry. Mother makes a big pot of soup. After lunch Bekzod runs out to play football, and Malika reads a book. Mother sits down with a cup of tea and smiles.

items.prompt: When did the grandfather make the garden?
items.audio:
Welcome to our garden! My grandfather made it twenty years ago, and now I help him every weekend. Come with me, and I will show you around.

We start at the gate. On the left you can see a long path with roses on both sides. They are red, white and yellow, and they smell lovely in June. My grandmother loves them, and she cuts some for the table every Friday.

In the middle of the garden there are fruit trees. We have two apple trees, one pear tree and a big old walnut tree. The walnut tree is my favourite, because I have a swing on it. In autumn we collect the fruit and put it in boxes. My grandmother makes jam and dried fruit for winter.

Behind the trees there is a vegetable bed. Grandfather grows tomatoes, cucumbers, onions and carrots there. He waters them every morning at seven o'clock, before it gets hot. I help him, but sometimes I water my shoes instead of the plants!

At the end of the garden there is a small wooden house for our hens. We have six hens, and they give us fresh eggs every day. Last, here is a bench under the vine. We sit here in the evening, drink tea and listen to the birds. Do you like our garden?

The present is a secret. Dilshod wants a blue bicycle, and his parents bought one last week. It is in the neighbour's garage. On Saturday morning Farhod is going to bring it home and hide it behind the tree. Mother is sure that Dilshod will be very surprised and happy.

items.prompt: Why are the children at home?
items.audio:
Today it is raining, so Kamola and her brother Ulugbek are at home. It is Sunday, and they cannot go to the park. At first they are bored. Ulugbek looks out of the window and says, "The rain is so heavy! I think it will not stop today."

Their mother has an idea. "Let us make a fun day at home," she says. First they build a tent in the living room with a big blanket and four chairs. Inside the tent there are pillows, a small lamp and a lot of books. Kamola reads a story about a dragon, and Ulugbek draws it.

At eleven o'clock they make pancakes in the kitchen. Ulugbek breaks the eggs, and Kamola mixes the flour and milk. Mother cooks them in a pan. They eat the pancakes with honey and strawberry jam. Ulugbek eats seven pancakes, and Kamola eats only three.

In the afternoon the children play a board game with Father. He is very bad at it and loses three times. Everybody laughs. Then Kamola calls her grandmother on the phone and tells her about their day.

At six o'clock the rain stops, and a rainbow appears in the sky. The children run to the window and look at it. Kamola says, "It was a boring morning, but it became a very good day."

items.prompt: How hot was it on Friday?
items.audio:
Last Friday it was thirty-six degrees, the hottest day of the summer. Nodira and her friends decided to go to the lake near the city. There were four girls: Nodira, Feruza, Shahlo and Mohira. They met at the bus station at nine o'clock and took a bus. The trip took forty minutes.

When they arrived, the lake was wonderful. The water was clear and blue, and there were green hills around it. They found a place under a big tree, put their towels on the grass and opened their bags. Feruza had water, Shahlo had melon, and Mohira brought sandwiches. Nodira had a big umbrella and sun cream.

The girls swam for an hour. The water was cold at first, but then it felt nice. After that they played volleyball on the sand with some boys. Their team lost, but they did not mind.

At one o'clock they ate lunch in the shade. The sun was very strong, so Nodira put on a hat and glasses. Shahlo forgot her hat and got a headache. She drank a lot of water and rested for a while.

The girls took a bus home at five o'clock. They were tired and a little red from the sun, but they were happy. They promised to come back next month.

items.prompt: What kind of holiday does Sherzod want?
items.audio:
Mister Sherzod Umarov wants a holiday for his family, so he calls a travel agency. A woman called Lola answers the phone. She says, "Good afternoon. How can I help you?" Sherzod says, "I would like a week by the sea in August."

Lola asks, "How many people are going?" Sherzod answers, "Four people. My wife, my two children and me. Our son is eight, and our daughter is twelve." Lola says, "I have a good hotel in Turkey. It is near the beach and has a big pool. The room has two beds and a small sofa."

Sherzod asks about the price. Lola says, "For seven nights, it costs one thousand eight hundred dollars for the whole family. Breakfast and dinner are included." Sherzod thinks for a moment and says, "That is a little expensive. Is there a cheaper hotel?" Lola answers, "Yes, there is another hotel, but it is a ten-minute walk from the beach. It costs one thousand five hundred dollars."

Sherzod likes the second hotel. He says, "We will take it. The flight leaves on the tenth of August, right?" Lola says, "Yes, at six o'clock in the morning. Please come to our office tomorrow with your passports." Sherzod thanks her and says goodbye.

items.prompt: How cold was it yesterday morning?
items.audio:
It is the first week of December, and the weather is getting very cold. Yesterday it was minus five degrees in the morning. Sevinch and her mother, Zulfiya, are talking about winter clothes in their bedroom.

Mother says, "Sevinch, your old coat is too small. We need to buy a new one." Sevinch is happy because she wants a long, dark blue coat. Mother says, "Good idea. Blue is a nice colour, and a long coat is warmer." Then she looks at the hats. "Your white hat has a hole. Let us buy a new wool hat too."

Sevinch asks, "And what about gloves?" Mother finds two pairs in the wardrobe. One pair is red, and the other one is black. Sevinch takes the red pair. Then she shows her boots. They are fine, but the socks are thin. Mother says, "We will buy three pairs of thick socks. Cold feet are no fun."

On Sunday they go to the market. The new coat costs eighty thousand sum, and the hat costs fifteen thousand. The seller is kind and gives them a small discount. Sevinch puts on her new coat and looks in the mirror. She says, "Thank you, Mum! Now I am not afraid of the cold." Mother smiles and says, "Please do not lose the gloves!"
